en: The Hymn to the Twelve Jyotirliṅgas

I take refuge in that Somanātha, who is composed of light, who wears the crescent moon as his crest-jewel, and who has compassionately descended into the most beautiful land of Saurāṣṭra for the sake of bestowing devotion. 1.
I take refuge in him who dwells with joy on the slopes of Śrīśaila, in the company of the gods, and also upon the lofty peak of Mount Tula.
I bow to that Arjuna, preceded by Mallika, the bridge across the ocean of saṃsāra. 2.

I salute Mahākāla, the great lord of the asuras, who manifested his descent in Avantikā for the sake of granting liberation to the virtuous and for the purpose of protecting them from untimely death. 3.
I praise the one Lord Śiva, the single Oṃkāra, who dwells eternally in Māndhātṛpura at the holy confluence of the Kāverī and Narmadā rivers for the sake of ferrying the virtuous across,
and who always resides in Prajvalikānidhāna in the northeast together with the Daughter of the Mountain.
I bow to that Śrī Vaidyanātha, whose lotus feet are worshipped by the gods and the asuras.
5 In the exceedingly beautiful city of Sadaṅga to the south, I take refuge in the one Lord Śrī Nāganātha, whose limbs are adorned with various enjoyments, who bestows true devotion and liberation. 6

I praise the one Lord Śiva, the sole Kedāra, who delights on the slope and shore of the great mountain, being constantly worshipped by the lords of sages, by gods, asuras, yakṣas, great serpents, and others;
he who dwells upon the pure summit of the Sahya mountain, in the holy region on the banks of the Godāvarī.
I praise that Lord Tryambaka, by the sight of whom sin is swiftly destroyed.

(8) I bow with constant devotion to him known as Rāmeśvara, who was established by Śrī Rāmacandra after he had built a bridge across the confluence of the waters of the Tāmraparṇī and the ocean using countless arrows. (9)
I bow to that Śaṅkara, who is beneficial to his devotees, who is constantly attended by assemblies of Ḍākinīs and Śākinīs as well as by flesh-eaters, and who is renowned by such names as Bhīma;
who dwells joyfully in Ānandavana, the root of bliss, and who has destroyed the multitude of sins. 10–11.
I take refuge in Śrī Viśvanātha, the Lord of Vārāṇasī, the protector of the protectorless.

(11) In this beautiful and vast city of Ilāpura, I take refuge in the one known as Ghṛṣṇeśvara, who shines forth as the most excellent in the world, whose nature is eternally most noble and generous. (12)
This hymn has been proclaimed in due order for the twelve Liṅgas composed of light, whose very nature is Śiva.
Having recited this with supreme devotion, a person should worship them constantly, beholding its fruit.
Thus ends the *Śrīdvādaśajyotirliṅgastotra*.
